text:
Olivia (Marketing): Hey finance - my bag was lost on the flight to Munich and I had to buy basics (toothbrush, a shirt) plus an airline 'delivery fee' of $18 to get the bag overnighted. Paid on my personal card. I have receipts but the kiosk gave a tiny paper slip for the toiletries. What do you need to reimburse?
expense-bot: Reminder: For lost luggage emergency purchases attach receipts and airline Property Irregularity Report (PIR) number. Small paper slips accepted with manager attestation.
Elaine (Finance): Sorry that happened. We reimburse emergency essentials up to $150 per traveler pending submission of the airline PIR and receipts. Airline compensation (if any) will be offset against reimbursement. We need: 1) receipts/photos of purchases, 2) PIR# from airline, 3) short explanation in the expense form. Cash slips are OK with manager attestation.
Olivia (Marketing): Uploaded photos: toiletries slip (faded), store receipt for shirt ($29.90), and my personal card posting for $47.90 total. Also attached airline email with PIR# PIR-445672.
Derek (Manager): I confirm Olivia lost luggage on work trip and approve emergency purchases. Adding note in approval system.
Elaine (Finance): Great. Two items: 1) The $18 airline delivery fee is reimbursable as an incidental. 2) If the airline reimburses you directly later, please notify us so we can adjust. We'll also mark the toiletries slip as 'accepted with manager attestation'.
Tom (Travel-ops): Filing a follow-up with the card provider - did the corporate card charge go through earlier? We saw a handful of failures on that carrier last month.
Olivia (Marketing): company card attempted but terminal error; resulted in delayed check-in and luggage transfer. I can forward the photo of the terminal message.
expense-bot: Expense created: "Emergency essentials - Munich" status: awaiting approval. Link: https://expenses.internal/reports/EXP-3421
Elaine (Finance): Processing note: we'll reimburse $47.90 now and code to MARKETING-TRAVEL. If airline pays you more than $47.90, we will reclaim the overpayment. Expect payment in 3-5 business days. Case #FIN-2026-210.
Olivia (Marketing): Thanks all - saved my presentation day. Will follow up if airline issues a reimbursement. :relieved:
